title: main-is-fast-forward-of-dev checks CONTAINMENT, not fast-forwardness — a rewind of main passes
description:
MEASURED 2026-09-15 in a local scratch repo, with the constructed git state asserted BEFORE
the verdict was read. Nothing was pushed to origin.

ci.yml:295 `main-is-fast-forward-of-dev` runs on every push to main and asserts exactly one
thing:

    git merge-base --is-ancestor "${{ github.sha }}" origin/dev

That is CONTAINMENT: "main's new HEAD is a commit dev already held". The job is NAMED
"main is fast-forward of dev", which is a strictly stronger property, and the job never
looks at where main WAS. `github.event.before` is not read.

THE HOLE. Rewind main to an older commit that is still on dev. The new HEAD is an ancestor
of origin/dev, so the guard is GREEN, while commits come OFF main:

    dev tip (c4)        = bbf1c8cefb827b7940aa0d44a06af41a9f6fbeba
    rewind target (c2)  = 2fbcd7973916f1817e167c11677f348443a0caca
    main after rewind   = 2fbcd7973916f1817e167c11677f348443a0caca   (asserted, not assumed)

    guard's check   `merge-base --is-ancestor c2 dev`  -> GREEN
    a real ff check `merge-base --is-ancestor c4 c2`   -> RED (c4 is not an ancestor of c2)

Both halves of prove-it-rejects and prove-it-accepts are already satisfied by this job: a
genuine promotion is green, the merge button is red. The case that finds it is the third
question -- does the NAME claim more than the BODY measures -- which neither half asks.

WHY IT MATTERS HERE SPECIFICALLY. The job's own comment says it is "the guard that matters
most for this repo specifically: main carries zero branch rules here, so nothing else stands
between a bad push and main". A rewind is precisely the bad push it is the last line against,
and it is the one shape it cannot see.

THE CLAIM IS REPEATED OUTSIDE THE BODY, WITHOUT THE CAVEAT. CLAUDE.md's repo profile names
the job as "main is fast-forward of dev" when explaining why the two promotion guards are
deliberately not required contexts. A reader takes the guarantee from the name.

FIX SHAPE. Also assert the OLD main is an ancestor of the new one -- `git merge-base
--is-ancestor "$BEFORE" "$AFTER"` -- skipping when before is all-zeros (branch creation).
Keep the containment check; it catches a different thing (a foreign commit). Two assertions,
two messages.

AND EXTRACT IT. The job is inline shell, so it is untestable by construction and has never
had a test; that is why this survived. Extract to scripts/ and drive both branches against
local fixture repos, the way test/readme-readback.test.ts now does for A4 (LCLI-510).

METHODOLOGY NOTE, from opum-marketplace, and it cost them two false verdicts: zsh reads the
`:r` in "$SHA:refs/heads/main" as a variable modifier and pushes a garbage refspec, and
double quotes do NOT protect it. Use ${SHA}:refs/heads/main or run under bash, and assert the
resulting git state before trusting any verdict -- otherwise a proof that a gate reported on
an object it never measured is itself a measurement of an object that was never built.

PROVENANCE. Found by generalising LCLI-510's review: opum-marketplace reported the identical
defect in their promotion-guards.yml (OMARK-58) and named this repo's guard as a likely second
host. Verified here rather than inherited. opum-cli-e2e independently hit the same class
(TASK-74): a required check named "qualification matrix vs the committed baseline" that has
not compared against a baseline since 2026-09-07.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A rewind of main to an older commit that is still on dev makes the guard RED, proved against a constructed local repo whose state is asserted before the verdict is read
A genuine fast-forward promotion is still GREEN, proved separately — the accepting half, not inferred from the rejecting one
A foreign commit on main (the merge-button case) is still RED, so the existing containment check is kept rather than replaced
The assertion lives in scripts/ with a test that drives every branch against local fixture repos, because inline workflow shell is untestable by construction and that is why this survived
The job name and CLAUDE.md's repo-profile reference both describe what the body actually measures, or the body is widened to match the name
